hartlib.name: Hartlib
hartlib.about: [WIP] One research chat across everything you subscribe to, with every answer cited.

explain.lead: Hartlib is one research chat over everything you subscribe to, for people who read professional briefings.
points: Answers plain-language questions with each claim linked to its page
Reads dense briefings, letters and official records for you
Lets publishers publish issues and invite client companies

silo.name: Silo
silo.about: Isolated computers for AI agents. Run untrusted code with a desktop and computer use, branch checkpoints, and diff states.

explain.lead: Silo gives your AI agents their own isolated computers that you can branch, diff and fold back like a Git repo.
points: Run each agent in its own machine with a terminal, desktop and computer use, away from your host
Fork a machine at any checkpoint to explore in parallel, let an agent run wild or share with a teammate
Review the state diff of any fork and fold the changes you want back into your main machine

lcu.name: LCU
lcu.about: Codex computer use, decoupled from the app, for usage inside any harness.

explain.lead: LCU lets AI agents outside the Codex app use Codex's computer control to work your desktop apps.
points: Read windows, click, type and take screenshots in desktop apps
Approve or deny each app the first time an agent tries to use it
Read and control Chrome tabs through the official extension

fjord.name: Fjord
fjord.about: [WIP] The power without the storm: Fjord connects your agents to everything they work with.

explain.lead: Fjord sits between your Claude Code sessions and GitHub, and brings you only what you need to know or decide.
points: Answer every Claude Code session's questions and plans from one page
Sort your GitHub inbox and CI by rules you write as sentences
Hand a failing check to the Claude Code session that can fix it

sic.name: Sic
sic.about: [WIP] Live fact-checking of political debates against official sources.

explain.lead: Sic checks the facts in French political debates against official sources, live or on replay.
points: Turns debate audio into text and names who is speaking
Picks out checkable claims and skips opinions and promises
Gives no verdict without a cited source and a precise link

lastdrop.name: lastdrop
lastdrop.about: Use any model as a built-in subagent in Claude Code, with a subscription or API key, and spread usage across your accounts.

explain.lead: lastdrop lets Claude Code call any model as its own subagent and spreads the work across your accounts.
points: Switches to the next model when one runs out of quota or can't start
Checks every command an agent runs instead of asking you to approve it
Shows usage left on each account and when it resets

harness-bench.name: harness-bench
harness-bench.about: Compares coding agent harnesses on the same model. Claude Code vs nanocode on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-rebench.

highlights.text: Refresh amontlabs.com when a release is published

journal.text: lastdrop subagents that hit a usage limit partway through now carry on, on another Claude account or the next model in line, instead of failing. Silo computers are now refused right away when connecting to an address not on their list, on any port.

harness-bench compared Claude Code with nanocode, an open-source agent, on the same model: on two sets of coding tasks, nanocode solved about as many at similar or lower cost. Silo added one page listing what agents ask for and copies waiting for review.

highlights.text: Post-merge review follow-ups: imported containers stay blocked, runner privacy check per job, clean stops
Post-merge review, container sharing and docs: keep an imported computer's image, import time limit, doc corrections
Post-merge review, forks and sharing: exports never carry memory

journal.text: Silo made sure exported computers never include their memory, and brought computer use back on older virtual machines. Fjord's Router summary now keeps finished threads until you clear them and shows whether linked pull requests merged or closed.

highlights.text: CI runner post-merge review: reap failed runner commands, count containers in the Linux budget
Containers phase CT6: export, import and Connections for container computers
Containers phase CT5: desktop and computer use for container computers

journal.text: lastdrop now starts each T3 Code thread on the Claude account with the most usage left, and moves it when that account runs out. Silo's container computers got a desktop, checkpoints, copies, a terminal and export. LCU fixed computer use missing in Claude Code.

highlights.text: Make the large-baseline subtraction test machine-independent
Containers phase CT3: secrets, GitHub access and published ports for container computers
Containers phase CT2: the container runtime core

journal.text: Silo added container computers on Linux, an opt-in kind labeled less isolated than its virtual machines, and can now run GitHub Actions jobs, each in a fresh computer. Fjord's Router now shows where a message will go before it is sent.

highlights.text: Forks phase F2: fork the source as it is now, desktop setting per computer
Forks phase F1: fork measurements before, plan and build log
Connections: name a blocked local network connection on a Mac

journal.text: Fjord's Router now works with T3 Code instead of Claude Code: it sends your words to T3 threads and brings their agents' questions to you. Silo can set up a Mac or Linux machine to host computers for another device, and a computer's desktop can now be turned off.

highlights.text: Silo 0.13.0: unsigned release path and version
Phase 4 credentials check passes live; correct the blocked-events doc
Launch drafts ready for review (0.13.0)

journal.text: Silo can now run agents' computers on a Linux machine and send commands and desktop control to computers on another device. Its app got screens to review an agent's changes. Fjord's Router can now send one message to several threads at once.

highlights.text: Silo v1 phase 2: review a fork's changes, keep them into main, undo
Silo v1 phase 1: silo CLI and MCP server, quiet forks, one-boot macOS forks, a URL per fork

journal.text: Silo can now show what an agent changed in a copy of its computer, keep those changes in the original, and undo that. Fjord's Router window became a running summary of every project, where questions waiting for you are answered by number or by typing.

highlights.text: release: fold guest image v5 into the 0.12.0 notes
Silo v1 phase 0: status reads during jobs, checkpoint disk that comes back, signing prep
release: prepare Silo 0.12.0

journal.text: Fjord's Router now picks which Claude Code project or thread on claude.ai each message is for and sends it there, and can offer to create a new project. Silo released 0.12.0, which adds macOS computers next to Linux ones.

highlights.text: fix(macos): make Edit CPU & memory work for local and remote computers
feat(computer-use): macOS computers use Cua Driver instead of ChatGPT and LCU
fix(launcher): register the engine again when launchd dropped its job

journal.text: Silo, which runs each AI agent in its own virtual machine, switched agents' desktop control from the ChatGPT app and LCU to an open-source tool, and added tests where an agent tries to break out. lastdrop stopped macOS asking for access to Music and Documents.

highlights.text: fix(build): keep Windows temp cleanup from failing the build

journal.text: LCU's build for Windows no longer fails at the very end when a temporary folder can't be deleted because another program is briefly holding a file in it.

highlights.text: fix(windows): extract the native-pipe host from webpack builds

journal.text: LCU's Windows installer, not yet officially supported, works again with current ChatGPT app versions, where it had stopped. lastdrop fixed a full agents list making every agent fail, and its panel now marks the account subagents will really go to next.
lastdrop got a website and a launch video. Its panel now lists each agent's backup models under it, and its account limit settings now cover Codex, Z.ai and OpenRouter too.

lastdrop added a Stats tab with token use and what it would cost at API prices, by day, project, account and model. An agent can now have backup models that run if the first can't start, and the app now updates itself.

highlights.text: lastdrop: redesign, multi-account pools and rename
fix(claude): write lcu.json beside the approval mod only when the fallback cannot find lcu

journal.text: lastdrop now takes several accounts for every provider and runs agents on Codex, Z.ai and OpenRouter on the one with the most usage left. LCU's Claude Code setup stopped saving a path tied to one machine, so a skills folder kept in a repository stays the same on every machine.

highlights.text: fix(claude): install the approval mod through a linked skills folder and keep update notices in organizations
fix(claude): keep lifecycle hooks quiet when the lcu server is not connected
fix(pi): write the local extension with a plain path so pi-bolt compile can compile it in

journal.text: lastdrop now moves a subagent that hits an account's usage limit to another Claude account with room, where it carries on. LCU stopped Claude Code from showing an error at the end of every turn when LCU wasn't connected.

lastdrop switched to running Claude Code's subagents on other Claude accounts that still have room, instead of opening a Claude window per account. It also let people set up their own agents on Codex, Antigravity, Z.ai or OpenRouter models, which Claude calls like its own.

lastdrop began as a menu bar app that shows how much usage is left on Claude, Codex, Antigravity, Z.ai and OpenRouter accounts. It also learned to open a separate Claude app window for each Claude account, and to show the limit resets each account can still use.

highlights.text: fix(claude): accept hooks without a prompt id (agent-team teammates)
fix(junie): send instructions on the first prompt when the relay starts late

journal.text: Fjord's Router now shows its answer as it is written, with its thinking and tool calls a click away. LCU fixed computer use for teammates in Claude Code agent teams, where every call had failed, and Junie on macOS now gets LCU's instructions from its first prompt.

highlights.text: Add experimental Junie harness adapter
fix(windows): complete a full install with the current Store app
fix(windows): accept a Store package installed on another drive

journal.text: LCU added experimental support for Junie, where the agent asks for each app and the person approves it with Touch ID or a password. On Windows, LCU now installs with the current ChatGPT Store app, including when that app is on another drive.

highlights.text: fix(update): show update notices to the person only

journal.text: Fjord now delivers every message the same way, through another chat the Claude app runs, whether the target is running or asleep, and shows each one going from sending to delivered. LCU's update notices now reach the person only, not the agent's model.
Fjord can now wake a Claude Code chat that the Claude app isn't running, so a message sent to it still goes through. Retrying a failed send now resends it as it was.

highlights.text: feat(adapters): add an experimental DeepSeek Harness plugin
fix(runtime): ignore a parent LCU's runtime environment and keep Claude's out
fix(browser): check every browser family in browser status; test ChatGPT 26.1013

journal.text: LCU added experimental support for DeepSeek Harness and stopped Hermes sessions from growing their prompt by about 3 KB every turn. In Fjord, each session the Router follows now shows a line on what it is about overall and one on what its latest turn did.

LCU fixed approvals in the Claude app, where answering the card for a new app could leave computer use waiting about 30 minutes, mostly in auto permission mode. Fjord's Router now checks more messages for parts meant for different sessions.

highlights.text: fix: a fresh install offers Enable Silo Engine instead of saying the engine bundle is missing
Publish the engine for Apple Silicon only, release silod 0.1.1, cut engine releases from main
Publish prebuilt silod as engine-v* releases; read the signer requirement at runtime

journal.text: Fjord can now split a message meant for several places into parts, shown as you type, and send each part where it belongs. LCU now keeps computer use working after the ChatGPT app updates itself on macOS.
A ready-made copy of Silo's engine can now be signed again and built into another app. Fjord's connection to Silo stopped tying up shared threads, which had made its automated tests hang.

In Fjord, highlighted items in the Router's brief now respond to the inbox's keyboard shortcuts, and the brief's past versions moved to a resizable side panel that stays as left between launches. Pressing Esc also stopped closing the window.

Fjord can now stop a running coding session or interrupt it with a new message, and each send checks whether an item should be archived or a session stopped. Silo can repair its access to the Mac's Keychain, and imported Macs now finish setup when one step fails.
